> **Capability note.** This file is the DEPRECATED custom-prompts twin
> (`--skills=codex-prompts`); `fathom init --skills=codex` writes the skill
> proper to `.agents/skills/fathom-doctor/SKILL.md`, the path Codex
> documents. `fathom doctor` itself is fully harness-agnostic — a
> git-native/CLI check identical whether Codex or Claude Code runs it.
> Since 2026-09-12 `hooks_installed` and `hooks_firing` give Codex REAL
> verdicts rather than `skipped: unverified` — a live headless session
> verified the descriptor (`docs/adoption/codex.md` §6). `hooks_installed`
> reads `$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json` (NOT `<repo>/.codex/hooks.json`, which
> codex-cli 0.153.1 does not load) and `hooks_firing` reads beats stamped
> `harness=codex` in `~/.fathom/hooks.jsonl`. `hooks_coverage` is advisory
> and never FAILs: Codex offers 12 events, fathom wires 7, and the row
> names the 5 it leaves alone with the reason for each. `skills_installed`
> reads `.agents/skills` and `gate_posture` states Codex's documented fail
> mode. `lefthook_gates` still applies —
> the pre-push `fathom verify` gate is identical for both harnesses. The
> six phase-O checks (`binding_file`, `guard_file`,
> `binding_modules_mounted`, `binding_module_readiness`,
> `guard_dead_scopes`, `guard_include_modules_unbound`) are ALSO
> harness-agnostic — they read `.fathom/modules.cue`/`.fathom/guard.cue`
> and query the daemon, independent of which harness's hooks would consume
> them; a Codex-side binding/guard is still config-checkable even though
> its PreToolUse channel has no equivalent to fire on.

## 1. Run it

```sh
fathom doctor --harness=$HARNESS --path $DIR --service $SERVICE
```

Omit any arg to use its default (`--harness=auto`, `--path` cwd, `--service`
resolved from the same candidate identities the hooks probe). Add `--json`
for machine output.

Exit codes: `0` no confirmed failure; `1` a real, fixable problem; `2` doctor itself
could not run (bad flags / unresolvable path) — not a verdict on the repo.

## 2. Read the report

`unknown` names unresolved project wrapper wiring. `timeout` names an unfinished
probe. Neither is PASS or FAIL; both count under `summary.skipped` in JSON.
Definite missing hooks still FAIL alongside uncertainty, and a daemon that does
not answer within 5 s remains FAIL. The Setup hook's `--brief` names FAIL,
TIMEOUT and UNKNOWN rows with separate counts and always exits 0. An unfinished
probe must never be summarized as a clean run.

Each row is `{name, status, reason, remedy}`. `skipped` is NOT `fail` and
NOT a guessed `pass` — it means doctor could not check that condition
(unreadable config, unreachable daemon, unresolvable home directory).
`warn` (phase O) is a real, observable condition worth attention (a dead
guard, a bound module below `servable`) that **never fails the exit
code** — report it as its own bucket, not folded into `pass` or `fail`.
Report `skipped` as "could not verify: `<reason>`," never collapsed into
either extreme.

Eighteen checks: `mcp_registration`, `daemon_reachable`, `binary_fresh`
(a LOCAL proxy — the running binary's own build vs `git rev-parse HEAD`;
mind the linked-worktree caveat doctor prints when it applies),
`hooks_installed`/`hooks_firing` (any VERIFIED harness — Claude Code and
Codex), `hooks_coverage` (advisory, never FAIL), `lefthook_gates`
(both harnesses), `stanza_present`, `skills_installed`, `config_valid`,
`obligations_served`, `surface_traffic`, and phase O's `binding_file`,
`guard_file`, `binding_modules_mounted`, `binding_module_readiness`,
`guard_dead_scopes`, `guard_include_modules_unbound` (all harness-agnostic
— see the capability note above).

## 3. Apply remedies — with explicit approval, one at a time

Every `fail` row's `remedy` is one command — but confirm with the operator
before running it, especially:

- **Daemon restarts** (`binary_fresh`, `surface_traffic` remedies) —
  never run `launchctl kickstart …` from an agent's own sandboxed session;
  hand the exact command to the operator to run in a real terminal.
- **Recompiles** (`obligations_served`'s `fathom compile --dry-run=false`)
  spend real tokens against a configured provider — confirm the spend first.

Re-run `fathom doctor` after any remedy instead of assuming it worked.

## 4. Tie-in check (once all-pass)

An all-pass checklist proves configuration, not that this session has
*loaded* it. Make one real tool call (`find_symbol` against a symbol you
know exists) — a connection error despite all-pass
means "restart this session" (the registration/schema-discovery restart
caveat), not another wiring change. Optionally time one `edit-hook`
invocation against the ≤150-token / well-under-5s budget
(`docs/design/coding-agent-excellence.md` §2) — regularly nearing the 5s
hook timeout is worth a `fathom observe`, not a shrug.
